runs: We’ve made the difficult decision to shut down Revue on January 18, 2023.

In January 2021, >x< acquired Revue as part of an ongoing commitment to enhancing the >x< experience for writers everywhere. Our goal has always been to make it easy for these writers to connect with their readers and future subscribers on >x<, opening up new opportunities for readers to better connect with writers and their content. Integrating Revue into >x< has provided a huge amount of value, informing new product features that give writers more options for connecting with their audiences.

This has been a hard decision because we know Revue has a passionate user base. We’re grateful to everyone who has used our service over the years, and hope we can continue to help you build a community with your readers on >x<.

q: Can I Post a creator’s Revue profile or newsletter issue?

runs: Yes, you can share either a profile or a specific newsletter issue through Posts. When composing a Post, add the link to the creator’s Revue profile or to a newsletter issue you’d like to share, and >x< will automatically generate a link preview of the creator’s newsletter or Revue profile.

q: Can I read a preview of a newsletter on >x< before subscribing?

runs: In your Home timeline, you can preview a newsletter from a Post that shows the creator’s newsletter. On the Post, click or tap to read a preview. You will then see the option to subscribe. If you already subscribe to the newsletter, you may not be asked to subscribe again.

FAQs for creators

q: How do I show a newsletter on my >x< profile?

runs: Showing a newsletter on a >x< profile lets people subscribe to a creator’s Revue newsletter directly from the creator’s >x< profile. Once the creator turns on the subscribe feature in Revue, people on >x< will see a module on the creator’s >x< profile that invites them to subscribe. The reader can automatically use it to subscribe through Revue. The purpose of the subscribe from profile feature is to provide people on >x< with information about the creator's newsletter, including the newsletter title, author, and subscription fee, if any. We do not permit this feature to be used as “clickbait” or for promoting external products or services, distributing offers or promotions, or similar activity.
: The email used to subscribe (including any email associated with a subscriber's >x< account) will be shared with the newsletter owner.

Any creator with a >x< account connected to their Revue newsletter can turn on the feature to let anyone on >x< subscribe to their newsletter from >x<. Readers who would like to subscribe to a newsletter can use the feature any time they see it on a creator’s >x< profile or on Posts from the creator or others in their timeline.

q: Is there another way to share my newsletter on >x< aside from my profile?

runs: Yes, you can share it through Posts. When composing a Post, add the link to your Revue profile, and >x< will automatically generate a link preview for you. If you want to show a specific issue of your newsletter instead, just add the link to the issue you want to show and >x< will generate a link preview of the issue. As with the subscribe from profile feature, we do not permit this feature to be used as "clickbait" or for promoting external products or services, distributing offers or promotions, or similar activity.

q: What if I have multiple >x< accounts and my Revue newsletter is connected to the wrong one?

runs: You can connect your newsletter to a >x< account other than the >x< account you used to log in to Revue by visiting the

page. First, you’ll need to click or tap Disconnect in the >x< card on the Integrations page on Revue. Then, go to >x< in a new tab on your browser, log out of the account you don’t want the Subscribe button to appear on, and log into the one you do want the Subscribe button to appear on. Come back to Revue, and click or tap on Connect now on the Integrations page. Once you’ve configured your Settings as described above, you can show your newsletter on your profile and this will appear on the most recent >x< account you connected.
